problem_description: Compute the average pressure per particle for a two-dimensional dam-break simulation with the rheological (rheo) particle model. The simulation is carried out in Lennard-Jones units and restricted to two dimensions, with the z-dimension limits explicitly defined from -0.1 to 0.1. It should use the atom style to be rheo. Boundary conditions must be fixed in the x-direction, shrink-wrapped in the y-direction, and periodic in the z-direction (f s p). Ghost atom communication must be modified to include velocity information (comm_modify vel yes), and Newton's third law for pairwise interactions must be turned off (newton off). A rectangular computational domain extending from -1 to 150 in the x-direction and -1 to 80 in the y-direction is created, in which a block of fluid particles is initially confined by rigid walls specifically mapped using boundary variables (xlo, xhi, ylo, yhi) and a spatial buffer (dx=3.0). The fluid particles (type 1) are placed on a hexagonal lattice with number density n=1.0, while the wall particles (type 2) form immobile boundaries surrounding the fluid region. Rheological status flags must be explicitly initialized to 0 for the fluid group and 1 for the rigid wall group. Fluid interactions are modeled using the rheo pair style with a cutoff distance of 2.2, artificial viscosity coefficient ζ=0.1, reference density ρ_0=1.0, and dynamic viscosity η=0.1. Particle masses are set to m_p=ρ_0/n=1.0 for the fluid and 2m_p for the walls. Gravity with magnitude 1×10^(-3) is applied in the negative y-direction to initiate the dam-break flow, and the timestep is chosen as Δt=0.1*/c_s/3 with c_s=1.0. It must use the fix command with 'all rheo ${cut} quintic 10 surface/detection coordination 22 8 rho/sum' alongside an explicitly defined linear equation of state (fix 3 all rheo/pressure * linear), which is required for computing the correct pressure. Additionally, four specific per-atom computes must be initialized for: local density, per-atom pressure, surface particle detection, and surface normal vectors in x and y. Wall particles are constrained to remain stationary, and two-dimensional motion is enforced throughout the simulation. Thermodynamic output detailing the step, time, kinetic energy, and pressure must be printed every 20 timesteps. The system is evolved for 50,000 timesteps. Throughout the simulation, atom trajectories alongside the specific computed per-atom arrays (density, surface flag, pressure, and surface normals) must be dumped to a custom file named atomDump every 200 timesteps.
